access_license_conditions.source_detail: Not corroborated by a direct fetch of any official terms-of-use page (all such attempts 403'd). Exact, citable license text: UNKNOWN.
access_license_conditions.value: No single authoritative license text was confirmed this session. Search-snippet synthesis states the underlying source collections are de-identified, open-access clinical collections usable for non-commercial academic purposes without IRB oversight, used under their respective source collections' open-access/CC terms. available_report_sections.source_detail: GitHub Awesome-Medical-Dataset page (full page read): "Comparison section contains prior patient information", "Indication section details symptoms", "Findings section lists radiological observations", "Impression section outlines the final diagnosis." Corroborated by WebSearch snippets independently.

compatibility_gaps_with_current_baseline.source_detail: src/data/schema.py, src/data/parsing.py, and reference/original_repository/FactMM-RAG/data/parse.py were all read directly this session to produce this list.
value: src/data/schema.py's ReportRecord models exactly two report text fields (finding, impression) plus image_paths, patient_id, study_id, dataset -- IU X-Ray's Comparison and Indication sections have no corresponding field today.

src/data/parsing.py's _ID_PATTERNS dict hard-codes exactly two dataset-specific regexes for extracting (patient_id, study_id) from image paths -- 'mimic-cxr': /(p\d+)/(s\d+)/ and 'chexpert': /(patient\d+)/(study\d+)/. Neither pattern will match IU X-Ray's file/directory layout (which was not itself confirmed this session -- UNKNOWN); IU X-Ray is not present in this dict at all, so a new entry (or a different extraction mechanism) would be required before this project's existing parser could ingest IU X-Ray.

The official FactMM-RAG data/parse.py (reference/original_repository/FactMM-RAG/data/parse.py) expects three separate line-oriented input files (image paths, findings, impressions) with one line per image, aligned by line number -- IU X-Ray's native distribution (per-report XML or the Kaggle CSV pair) does not match this line-oriented convention and would need a new conversion step, not yet written by this project.

differences_from_mimic_cxr_chexpert.source_detail: The MIMIC-CXR/CheXpert-side figures cited for comparison are drawn from this project's own already-committed Cell 37/40 artifacts (OFFICIAL_REPOSITORY/PAPER_EXPLICIT sourced there, not re-derived here), not re-fetched this session.
value: Scale: 7,470 images / 3,955 reports (IU X-Ray) vs. this project's own recorded MIMIC-CXR figures of 125,417 train / 991 valid / 1,624 test image-report pairs (Cell 37, PAPER_EXPLICIT) -- roughly two orders of magnitude smaller.

Report schema: four sections (Comparison, Indication, Findings, Impression) vs. this project's MIMIC-CXR/CheXpert baseline schema, which models exactly two sections (finding, impression) -- see compatibility_gaps below.

Access: IU X-Ray sources read/searched this session describe no PhysioNet-style credentialed Data Use Agreement, unlike MIMIC-CXR's confirmed PhysioNet account + CITI training + signed DUA requirement (resource_inventory.json, Cell 40) and CheXpert's Stanford AIMI account registration requirement (same file).

No CheXpert-labeler-style bundled structured image labels were found described for IU X-Ray by any source read this session -- UNKNOWN whether any official or de-facto-standard CheXbert/RadGraph-style label set exists for it.

expected_download_size.value: Kaggle mirror (PNG images + CSV metadata): approximately 14GB total. Official NLM NLMCXR_png.tgz / NLMCXR_reports.tgz archive sizes: UNKNOWN.

image_count.source_detail: GitHub Awesome-Medical-Dataset page (full page read), corroborated independently by all four WebSearch queries this session.

image_formats.source_detail: DICOM/PNG conversion detail from the GitHub Awesome-Medical-Dataset page (full page read); the official-archive filename detail is WEBSEARCH_SNIPPET only.
image_formats.value: Kaggle/community mirror: PNG, converted from original DICOM (top/bottom 0.5% of DICOM pixel values clipped, linearly scaled to 0-255, shorter side resized to 2048px). Official NLM archive filename (NLMCXR_png.tgz, per WEBSEARCH_SNIPPET) implies PNG is also the format of the official distribution, but this was not independently confirmed by a direct fetch. Original source modality: DICOM.

image_to_report_relationship.source_detail: The <parentImage> XML tag detail comes from a WebSearch synthesis referencing community loader scripts (omar-mohamed/X-Ray-Report-Generation's get_iu_xray.py), not a direct fetch of that script this session.
image_to_report_relationship.value: Many-to-one and variable: a single report may have more than one associated image (e.g. frontal + lateral views). The official NLM XML report format identifies associated images via a <parentImage id="image-id"> tag per search-snippet evidence. Exact per-report min/max image counts: UNKNOWN. Average is approximately 1.89 images per report, computed here as 7470 / 3955 -- a derived arithmetic figure, not a dataset-stated statistic.

known_public_splits.source_detail: Split counts table from the GitHub Awesome-Medical-Dataset page (full page read). The "70/10/20, Li et al. 2018 origin, R2Gen-adopted" characterization is WEBSEARCH_SNIPPET only -- Li et al. 2018 itself was not fetched/read this session. This is NOT an official NLM-sanctioned split; it is a community convention.
known_public_splits.value: No official NLM-published train/val/test split was found. A de facto community-standard split (70%/10%/20%, patient-level) originating from Li et al. 2018 is widely reused across the literature, including R2Gen and its variants (e.g. R2Gen-Mamba). One community reproduction (the GitHub Awesome-Medical-Dataset page) reports concrete counts: train 5,226 images / 2,770 reports; validation 748 images / 395 reports; test 1,496 images / 790 reports.

metadata_format.source_detail: CSV filenames from the GitHub Awesome-Medical-Dataset page (full page read); XML/<parentImage> detail from WebSearch snippet only (not independently fetched).
metadata_format.value: Two distinct distributions observed: (1) official NLM NLMCXR_reports.tgz uses per-report XML files with a <parentImage id="..."> tag linking images to reports (WEBSEARCH_SNIPPET); (2) the Kaggle/community mirror instead provides two flat CSV files, indiana_projections.csv and indiana_reports.csv (WEBFETCH_PAGE_READ). These are two different repackagings of the same underlying data, not two conflicting facts about one format.

official_dataset_name.source_detail: Consistent across all four WebSearch queries this session; the underlying publication (Demner-Fushman et al., "Preparing a collection of radiology examinations for distribution and retrieval", cited as PubMed ID 26133894) was identified via search snippet and via the WEBFETCH_PAGE_READ GitHub page's own citation, but the paper itself was not fetched/read this session.
official_dataset_name.value: Indiana University Chest X-Ray Collection ("IU X-Ray"), distributed via the National Library of Medicine's Open-i (Open Access Biomedical Image Search Engine) service -- commonly referred to as "Open-I" or "IU X-Ray" interchangeably in the literature.
